Optimal.Notes: The 40 Hz refresh and frame cap deliver a fluid, tear-free experience that suits the parkour gameplay; FSR at a mild upscale ratio keeps image quality acceptable while giving the GPU headroom to hold the cap through horde encounters. Automatic GPU clock lets the driver respond to scene complexity.

profiles.Summary: Dying Light runs well on the Steam Deck thanks to its Verified status and strong Proton compatibility, with the RDNA 2 GPU sitting comfortably above the minimum GTX 560 spec. Expect a stable 30–40 fps at medium settings without upscaling, or a smoother 40+ fps experience with FSR and reduced settings.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended specs relative to the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU (roughly GTX 1050 Ti class, comfortably above the GTX 560 minimum). On your first run, check frame pacing in the Slums district and during zombie hordes — those are the most GPU-demanding scenarios — and adjust the profile up or down accordingly.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at a sub-native resolution with FSR upscaling keeps the GPU well under budget; the 8 W TDP cap and locked 30 fps give maximum battery longevity while remaining playable. Motion blur and DoF are disabled to reduce GPU load and improve perceived clarity at low resolution.

KnownIssues: Some players report occasional stutters during heavy zombie horde encounters in dense urban areas.
The game may require accepting the Easy Anti-Cheat prompt on first launch; multiplayer/co-op functionality may be limited under Proton.
HDR and some advanced post-processing options may not function correctly under Proton.
First-time shader compilation can cause stutters early in a session until the cache warms up.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Native 1280×800 with high textures looks sharp on the Deck's screen; expect 55–60 fps in open rooftop areas but dips toward 45 fps during large outdoor horde fights — consider dropping shadows to Low if dips are frequent. Battery life is short at full TDP, so keep a charger nearby for long sessions.

Optimal.Notes: A 45 Hz refresh rate with a matching frame cap delivers smooth, judder-free motion that feels better than an unlocked 40–55 fps swing. Medium textures and shadows keep the post-apocalyptic city looking solid while staying within the Deck's GPU budget.

profiles.Summary: Dying Light runs well on the Steam Deck OLED thanks to its Platinum ProtonDB rating, with the RDNA 2 GPU sitting comfortably between the minimum and recommended GPU specs, making 40–60 fps achievable at medium settings. No launch options are typically required and the game's full controller support makes it a great handheld experience.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended specs relative to the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU (roughly GTX 1050 Ti class, sitting between the GTX 560 minimum and GTX 780 recommended). On your first run, check frame rate in a busy street or rooftop chase sequence — if it dips below your cap, drop to the Optimal or Max Battery profile.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling keeps GPU load minimal; locking to 30 fps and capping TDP to 8 W maximizes session length. Motion Blur and Depth of Field disabled to reduce GPU overhead and improve clarity at lower resolution.

KnownIssues: Some users report occasional stuttering during large open-area traversal due to streaming/asset loading.
Anti-aliasing options may cause visual artifacts at lower resolutions under Proton.
HDR output may not be fully functional under Proton/Linux without additional configuration.
Co-op multiplayer sessions may have occasional connectivity issues under Proton.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Native 1280x800 with high textures and full TDP gives the best image quality the Deck can sustain; expect dips toward 45 fps in dense zombie hordes or wide outdoor areas. Battery life will be short, so this profile is best for plugged-in or short sessions.
